narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Slightly cooler and windier and much cloudier than yesterday. Showery, with thunder possible from midday, peaking this evening. 31°C / 89°F high, 20°C / 67°F low. Sky mostly cloudy early as reported, partly cloudy at midday and mostly cloudy in the evening. Wind NE early and SSW at midday; gusts to 37 km/h (20 kt). UV index 9.5 (very high). Air quality 45 (good) at Kisumu Airport, the highest of 3 stations. As of 06:03, reports through 04:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 25°C / 77°F; low so far 22°C / 72°F; peak sustained 9 km/h; sky mostly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS. The sky will be Mostly cloudy on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, Partly cloudy on Monday, and Mostly cloudy thereafter through Thursday. Friday sees four of four models wet with rain totals between 0.9 and 11.8 mm, a high of 29–31 °C and thunder likely. Saturday is also four of four wet, 9.5–25.9 mm, high 26–30 °C, thunder likely. Sunday remains four of four wet, 3.0–22.8 mm, high 28–29 °C, thunder likely. Day+3 (Sunday) high range 28–29 °C; Day+7 (Thursday) high range 30–31 °C. Record: Day+3 best rain record Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD), right 75 % of the last 30 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

The peak CAPE values indicate a strong thunderstorm potential today, with Best Match, ECMWF, ICON and UKMO all above the thunderstorm threshold and a peak at 18:00. Any thunderstorm could bring sudden gusts well above the forecast wind, exceeding the 37 km/h (20 kt) peak gust. No official warning has been issued by the Kenya Meteorological Department.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winam Gulf wind will be east-northeasterly overnight at 5 km/h (3 kt) gusting 10 km/h (5 kt), turning south-southwesterly by midday at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 19 km/h (10 kt), and into the evening at 13 km/h (7 kt) gusting 19 km/h (10 kt); peak gust 29 km/h (16 kt). Thunder is possible this evening, so gusts could briefly exceed the stated values.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1008 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1016 hPa) — an 8 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the southwest — a large-scale feature building in that direction. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Basin pressure today ranges from 1012.2 to 1014.3 hPa, near-steady over three days (+0.8 hPa). The call notes a pressure trend of +1.5 hPa, with the lowest pressure toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

The REVIEW notes that at Day+0 no model is meaningfully better than the others, and that Best Match slightly under-forecasts peak wind. The RECORD shows the ECMWF holds the best rain record for Day+0, yet the call’s rain amount (8.3 mm) aligns more closely with Best Match’s 5.1 mm than ECMWF’s 3.2 mm, placing ECMWF on the wrong side of its own record. KMD forecasts a maximum of 30 °C, slightly lower than the call’s 31 °C high, but otherwise agrees on the rain probability. DATA SUFFICIENCY indicates 47 checks for Day+0, providing a settled picture despite uneven coverage, and 16 checks for Day+3, enough for model comparison. Overall confidence is moderate, with slight uncertainties in wind and rain magnitude.
